{{Quote|The name's Tirog, and I'm a bounty hunter. That means I'll take most any job, if the risks are worth the money.|Tirog|<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />}}
'''Tirog''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] active during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A skilled marksman, [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], and hunter, he frequently found himself in the midst of combat and conflict during his eventful career.

Tirog was notable for his wide range of acquaintances, associates, and contacts, who included the same sort of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] other bounty hunters considered to be targets. At times, he was accompanied by one or more companions, most frequently his [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], [[GT-9R]], or "Niner." Other frequent associates included the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Drebble]] and a child who called himself "[[Ace (kid)|Ace]]." In other recorded incidents, Tirog appeared to have been working alone. He also had many enemies, ranging from criminals to local government figures. Though he considered himself neutral during the war, Tirog found himself battling the forces of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] on numerous occasions.

==Biography==
The biography of Tirog, a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]], consisted primarily of incomplete, disconnected anecdotes about his career as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], the sequence of which was not always clear. Most of these anecdotes involved brushes with danger, such as operating an [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]] [[Walker/Legends|walker]] while avoiding fire from a [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]], commanding a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]]-sized group of forty soldiers, getting involved in a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] chase that ended in a collision, firing his [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter's]] weapons at a speeder, or attacking a [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]] flying overhead.<ref name="Second Edition" /> It appeared he came out on top most of the time, and managed achievements that could be described as heroic.<ref name="Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game">In ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', "[[The Force/Legends|Force]] points" are given out to player characters who have achieved heroic or dramatic deeds during the course of an adventure. The second edition rulebook uses Tirog as an example of a character who has the maximum number of Force points allowed for a character who is not [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].</ref> He did not always meet with unqualified success, however. He was once forced to flee from a mob of angry [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]],<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> and when lost in the [[Yar'En]] region of [[Goroth Prime/Legends|Goroth Prime]] without supplies, suffered from debilitating cramps and nausea from eating the native [[Moss/Legends|mosses]].<ref name="Goroth">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref>

===Tirog versus the Empire===
While traveling together, Tirog and GT-9R found themselves in the office of Imperial [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Dermeg]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ansillivog]]. While in Dermeg's office, the governor accused Tirog of working for known criminals, consorting with Rebels, and committing crimes against the Empire for pay. During this interview, the governor threatened to have Tirog summarily executed.<ref name="Second Edition" />

Whatever the details of these alleged crimes or the truth of Dermeg's allegations, Tirog was involved in at least two recorded firefights against Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] personnel. He also tangled with the forces of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], once trying to escape three [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] while at the controls of a [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]]. His [[Starship/Legends|ship]] was also captured by the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] of an [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] at one point, though this may have been during the same incident.<ref name="Second Edition" />

===Tirog versus local authorities===
[[File:Tirog_shooting.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Tirog aiming his [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]]]

Tirog also frequently found himself at odds with local authorities. While on a mission to the planet [[Besero/Legends|Besero]] on behalf of the [[Tagge Mining Company|Tagge Mining Corporation]], Tirog was treated as a nuisance by the local bureaucracy&mdash;not due to his own actions, but because Tagge had caused them so many problems in the past. Tirog himself came into conflict with the authorities on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] on several occasions, making it difficult to get their cooperation when he revisited the desert world.<ref name="Second Edition" />

Neither of these conflicts seem to have been as serious as his problems with the [[Gettiarn Space Station]] administration, however. While visiting that station with GT-9R, three armed guards leveled their [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]] at the hunter and his droid, demanding their surrender. Though GT-9R suggested negotiation, Tirog pulled out his own blaster rifle instead and returned fire.<ref name="Second Edition" />

===Tirog versus the underworld===
Tirog also made enemies in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] underworld. For example, Tirog and GT-9R once ran afoul of the loan shark and crimelord [[Ploovo Two-For-One/Legends|Ploovo Two-For-One]]. Ploovo tried to set up an ambush for the hunter and his droid, but the element of surprise was lost when Tirog and Niner captured two of Ploovo's agents and learned about his plans.<ref name="Second Edition" />

Another confrontation with the underworld occurred when Tirog, Ace, Drebble, and GT-9R visited an open-air marketplace on a world with a bright blue [[Star/Legends|sun]]. During this visit, they were accosted by a [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] accompanied by two armed thugs, who had been pursuing the group for some time. When the gambler and his cronies prepared to fire on the foursome, Tirog fired back. His counterattack immediately killed one of the gambler's thugs and stunned the other. Tirog's companions were not so effective in the skirmish, with GT-9R and Ace taking refuge in a nearby [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] and Drebble hesitating too much to take any action.<ref name="Second Edition" />

===Tirog's associates===
Tirog claimed to have dealt with people ranging from a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to a Wookiee [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] in the course of his career.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> Not all of them became Tirog's enemy, of course. He frequently met with friendly contacts, such as the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter [[Reeveid]], in cantinas.<ref name="Second Edition" /> He was on good enough terms with smugglers such as [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] and the [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilot]] [[Evinn Dastt]] to ask them for favors. When an unidentified individual paid Tirog to act as a "guide to the galaxy" for one or more novices, Okeefe and Dastt helped him give lessons.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

GT-9R, Ace, and Drebble&mdash;his most common traveling companions&mdash;helped him out on several occasions. For example, Drebble once tried to repair a [[Power coupling/Legends|power coupling]] on Tirog's ship at double speed in order to hurry them off-world, while Ace once rushed to Tirog's aid when the hunter was knocked unconscious by a [[Stun/Legends|stun]] bolt from a stormtrooper's blaster. GT-9R may have been his closest associate, or at least his most frequent companion, despite their clashing personalities. While Tirog was a rough-and-tumble sort eager to fight in a crisis, GT-9R was a somewhat snobbish droid whose programming led him to avoid combat, sometimes attempting negotations in the middle of a firefight.<ref name="Second Edition" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Drop your weapons and surrender!''"<br />"''I'll drop ''you'', not my weapons.|Gettiarn Space Station guards and Tirog|<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />}}
[[File:TirogSquint.png|thumb|right|120px|Tirog]]

Tirog was a man of action, used to a violent and adventurous lifestyle. He was comfortable in disreputable cantinas like the [[Dancing Dewback]], which he called "a good bar fight waiting to happen." His first instinct when confronted was to try and fight his way out. This was in direct contrast to many of his acquaintances. Some, like Ace and GT-9R, were non-combatants who usually tried to get out of the way when blasters started firing.<ref name="Second Edition" /> Others, such as his smuggler acquaintances Platt Okeefe and [[Blaine Hansom]], would try to talk their way out of trouble: a practice Tirog called a "waste of effort."<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

While Tirog seemed to enjoy combat, he had seen too much to have any illusions about it, and believed that people without the courage or experience to handle themselves in a fight were better off staying clear. He gave novices two pieces of advice: first, "don't get shot," and second, "always have a [[Medpac/Legends|medpac]] or two&hellip;or three." Tirog saw the galaxy as a whole as a dangerous place, where some familiarity with weapons and combat was necessary for survival.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> He also knew enough not to enter potentially dangerous situations unprepared. When entering the Dancing Dewback with GT-9R to meet with a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] contact, he made sure to check for potential entrances and exits and any heavily armed patrons before proceeding.<ref name="Second Edition" />

During the Galactic Civil War, Tirog described himself as someone in the "middle," affiliated with neither the Rebel Alliance nor the Galactic Empire. While he disliked the Empire, describing the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] as no better than armed thugs, he was pessimistic about the Alliance's chances in the war.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> Nevertheless, he did have at least four separate violent encounters with Imperial forces,<ref name="Second Edition" /> and was a known associate of Rebels like Platt Okeefe and Evinn Dastt.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

Tirog had a completely shaved head, save for a long fringe of hair at the back reaching past his shoulders. This fringe was mostly white, with red coloring at the ends. He sported several [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoos]]: red markings on his right forearm and temple, and a purple design surrounding his right eye.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

==Skills and abilities==
Tirog was an expert with blasters, especially [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]]. He once sharpened his skills by training with a marksman named [[Hist]]. After a week's training, Tirog had equaled his teacher's skill.<ref name="Second Edition" />

Tirog was also skilled in piloting [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicles and [[Freighter/Legends|space transports]], especially [[Ghtroc Industries/Legends|Ghtroc Industries]] light freighters. As an able bounty hunter, he was also proficient at searching for hidden objects and individuals, and at avoiding blaster bolts and other weapons fire. Though Tirog was not an expert [[sentientologist]], he knew a good deal about Wookiees.<ref name="Second Edition" />

In the course of his career, Tirog took care to improve his skills&mdash;and not just his combat skills. As time wore on, he learned to drive a hard bargain in the marketplace, and became more generally knowledgeable than he had been as a rookie.<ref name="Second Edition" /> According to Tirog, his wide range of acquaintances, friendly and otherwise, meant he knew how different people would react to a given situation.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

==Equipment==
Tirog owned a battered Ghtroc Industries light freighter&mdash;possibly a [[720 light freighter/Legends|Class 720 freighter]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition">While ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition]]'' only identifies his ship as a "Ghtroc freighter," the Class 720 freighter is the only Ghtroc freighter described in that rulebook.</ref> He had some smuggler "friends" customize his ship in return for letting them go free, reasoning that the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on their heads was worth less than the ship's modifications.<ref name="Second Edition" />

Tirog's personal equipment included a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]], a pair of [[Macrobinoculars/Legends|macrobinoculars]], a [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]], and two medpacs. His arsenal included a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]], a [[Light repeating blaster/Legends|light repeating blaster]], a blaster rifle, a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|holdout blaster]], and a [[Knife/Legends|knife]]. He also used a [[Vibro-ax/Legends|vibro-ax]] at one point.<ref name="Second Edition" /> Tirog typically wore light [[Armor/Legends|armor]] including a [[Blast vest/Legends|protective vest]] and leg armor.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> During his time with Ace, Niner, and Drebble, he carried about 800 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] in cash.<ref name="Second Edition" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition''===
{{Quote|The two goons will each ''dodge'' and then open fire, one shot each, on Tirog &hellip;''"<br />"''Why always me? Can I ''dodge''?''"<br />"''Nope; too late.|"Bill" and "Greg" in "Tirog's Story: Five"|<ref name="Second Edition" />}}
[[File:IotranBountyHunter-SWRPG2E.png|thumb|right|120px|Tirog's game statistics are based on the [[Iotran/Legends|Iotran]] "Bounty Hunter" sample character template, illustrated here.]]
Tirog's first appearance is as a sample character in "Tirog's Story," a series of gameplay examples in [[Bill Smith]]'s [[1992]] roleplaying game book [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]], published by [[West End Games]]. "Tirog's Story" covers the creation of Tirog as a player character, the setup for a meeting with Reeveid, a confrontation in a marketplace, with Ace, Drebble, and GT-9R appearing as other player characters, to provide a simple combat example, and an example of skill use&mdash;Tirog's failed attempt to fix a broken droid. Other short examples of combat and skill use throughout the rulebook refer to Tirog. Tirog's player in "Tirog's Story" is identified as "Greg," while the gamemaster in "Tirog's Story" is named "Bill."

Appendix One of the rulebook, "Roleplaying Basics," contains more roleplaying examples featuring Tirog. In these examples, Bill, Greg, and "Ted" (GT-9R's player) play through Tirog and GT-9R's meeting with a contact in the Dancing Dewback, their confrontation with Governor Dermeg, and an encounter with guards on Gettiarn Space Station. It also describes Bill's setup of a conflict between Tirog, GT-9R, and Ploovo Two-for-One as an example of an ongoing villain who is unaware of the players' plans. Tirog's second appearance, in [[Nigel D. Findley]]'s sourcebook ''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]'', is also an example of game mechanics—in this case, an illustration of the debilitating effects of eating Goroth Prime's native plant life when nothing more edible is available.

Tirog's game statistics and equipment are based on the "Bounty Hunter" character template in the second edition rulebook. Though the template in that rulebook is for an [[Iotran/Legends|Iotran]] character, Tirog is later depicted as a Human in Smith's [[1996]] game book, ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''.

===''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded''===
{{Quote|Hey, gamemastering isn't that hard&mdash;and after outrunning a bunch of Wookiees determined to pull my arms out of their sockets, I know what I'm talking about.|Tirog, advising beginner gamemasters|<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />}}
In the ''Revised and Expanded'' rulebook, Tirog appears along with Platt Okeefe, [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]], and various other characters in order to introduce the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe and the rules of the game to players. Though Tirog and the other characters remain in character, they "[[Wikipedia:Fourth wall|break the fourth wall]]" by addressing the readers directly and discussing the rules of the game. Tirog, for example, claims to have been paid to act as a "guide to the galaxy" for readers. Tirog appears in the introduction, chapter 3 ("How to Gamemaster"), and chapter 5 ("Combat and Injuries.")

Tirog himself does not appear in the revised rulebook's gameplay examples. GT-9R does appear, but as part of a different group of player characters. This group includes [[Thannik]], another bounty hunter character played by Greg. This gameplay example is identical with the "Dancing Dewback" scene in the previous rulebook, but with Thannik replacing Tirog and several other player characters added. Thannik's creation as a player character in the revised rulebook is also nearly identical to the character creation sections of "Tirog's Story." Several other examples of gameplay involving Thannik appear to be rewritten versions of the earlier rulebook's examples involving Tirog, including a passage where Tirog's associate Drebble fixes Thannik's ship.
